blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — basal insulin glargine administration
stem: A client is prescribed insulin glargine (LANTUS) as basal insulin. Which administration teaching is correct?

options.A: Inject LANTUS subcutaneously once daily at a consistent time each day, and do not mix or dilute it with another insulin or solution.
options.B: Use LANTUS as a rapid mealtime bolus before carbohydrate-containing meals because its primary role is to cover the immediate postmeal glucose rise.
options.C: Administer LANTUS intravenously for diabetic ketoacidosis because the long-acting formulation is preferred for rapid correction of severe insulin deficiency.
options.D: Mix LANTUS in the same syringe with another insulin before injection so both basal and mealtime insulin effects can be delivered in one preparation.

rationale: Current LANTUS prescribing information directs subcutaneous administration once daily at any time of day but at the same time every day and states not to dilute or mix LANTUS with any other insulin or solution. LANTUS is a long-acting basal insulin and is not recommended for treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis. Therefore A is correct. B misclassifies it as a rapid mealtime insulin, C uses an inappropriate route and indication, and D directly conflicts with the no-mixing instruction.
educational_objective: Teach correct basal insulin glargine administration: once-daily subcutaneous dosing at a consistent daily time without mixing or diluting it with another insulin or solution.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_document_title: LANTUS (insulin glargine) injection — Full Prescribing Information
source_version_date: Prescribing information revised May 2025; current DailyMed label verified and accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Indications and Usage §1 — not recommended for diabetic ketoacidosis; Dosage and Administration §2.1/§2.2 — administer subcutaneously once daily at any time of day but at the same time every day; do not dilute or mix with any other insulin or solution.
source_claim_supported: LANTUS is administered subcutaneously once daily at the same time each day, should not be diluted or mixed with other insulin or solution, and is not recommended for DKA treatment.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: prepare and administer medications safely; educate client about medications; evaluate medication response.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete insulin-administration strategies without the original absolute-word cue.
Balanced option length and combined the two key label-supported administration rules in the correct answer.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current LANTUS administration labeling. The correct option is not longest; B-D are plausible insulin-use errors but clinically distinct and clearly incorrect.
